title: Comparing and Evaluating Changepoint Methods with ggchangepoint
text: single changepoint detection method dominates across signal shapes, noise regimes, computational budgets: large-scale evaluations find ranking algorithms highly dataset-dependent default configurations often far optimal (van den Burg Williams 2020; Truong et al. 2020). Sound practice therefore requires running several detectors, comparing outputs, — ground truth available — scoring well-defined accuracy metrics. article presents comparison evaluation toolkit ggchangepoint: visual comparison across methods (ggcpt_compare()), common tidy representation competing segmentations (ggcpt_compare_table()), metrics module implementing precision/recall/F1 one--one matching, covering metric, Hausdorff distance, adjusted Rand index (cpt_metrics()), multi-annotator scoring style Turing Change Point Dataset benchmark (cpt_metrics_annotated()), visual evaluation ground truth (ggcpt_eval()). discuss three complementary tools quantifying uncertainty segmentation — engine-native confidence intervals, bootstrap stability profiles (cpt_stability()), CROPS penalty path (cpt_crops()) — close small simulation-based benchmarking workflow built package’s ground-truth generators.

title: Comparing and Evaluating Changepoint Methods with ggchangepoint
text: changepoint literature offers wide menu detectors — penalised optimal partitioning, binary segmentation wild narrowest--threshold refinements, moving-sum statistics, nonparametric divergence measures, Bayesian posteriors — inductive bias (Aminikhanghahi Cook 2017; Truong et al. 2020). Benchmarks score many algorithms many series find uniform winner: performance depends kind change (mean, variance, distribution), noise (Gaussian, heavy tailed, autocorrelated), number spacing changes, tuning penalties thresholds (van den Burg Williams 2020). Two practical consequences follow. First, analyst compare several methods data hand rather trust one default. Second, ground truth (expert annotation) exists, comparison quantitative, using metrics agreed conventions. ggchangepoint supports activities behind one interface. Every detector returns tidy ggcpt object, competing methods directly comparable; comparison module renders side side, evaluation module scores . article package’s methods-paper treatment workflow. companion vignette vignette("introduction", package = "ggchangepoint") documents full detection surface; take detectors given focus comparison, evaluation, uncertainty.

text: package’s simulation module closes loop: generators known truth feed metrics module, methods can scored replications. cpt_simulate() draws series specified changepoints, canonical test signals ship ready-made generators — including signal_blocks(), Donoho–Johnstone blocks signal (Donoho Johnstone 1994), plus signal_teeth() signal_stairs().  minimal benchmark: three methods, ten replications two-change series, scored precision, recall, F1, covering. (clarity keep everything sequential small; cpt_batch() runs one method many series honours future::plan() parallel execution larger studies.) Mean accuracy 10 replications (margin = 5). skeleton scales studies van den Burg Williams (2020): generators (heavy-tailed autocorrelated noise via cpt_simulate(noise = "t") noise = "ar1"), methods (everything cpt_methods()), replications, parallel execution via future::plan(multisession).

title: Comparing and Evaluating Changepoint Methods with ggchangepoint
text: Comparison evaluation afterthoughts changepoint analysis; analyst earns confidence segmentation. design ggchangepoint’s toolkit follows three principles. First, common representation makes comparison trivial: every engine returns ggcpt contract location convention, ggcpt_compare() metrics module work thirty-plus methods without special cases. Second, metrics must agree pictures: ggcpt_eval() cpt_metrics() share one matching routine, plotted true positive counted true positive. Third, uncertainty deserves first-class treatment: engine-native intervals, bootstrap stability, penalty paths give three independent views much reported changepoint trusted, three render directly ggplot2 (Wickham 2016). detection surface — dispatcher, engine wave, Bayesian displays, multivariate tools — see vignette("introduction", package = "ggchangepoint") feature tour vignette("ggchangepoint", package = "ggchangepoint").

text: Multiscale inference confidence. SMUCE (Frick et al. 2014) heteroskedastic extension HSMUCE (Pein et al. 2017) control probability -estimating number changes return confidence interval every changepoint location (ci_lower/ci_upper): Change slope. CPOP performs exact penalised estimation continuous piecewise-linear mean (Fearnhead et al. 2019; Fearnhead Grose 2024): Bayesian detection. bcp_wrapper() implements Barry–Hartigan product-partition model (Barry Hartigan 1993; Erdman Emerson 2007) reports posterior probability per location; bocpd_wrapper() runs Bayesian online changepoint detection run-length posterior (Adams MacKay 2007); beast_wrapper() wraps BEAST Bayesian model-averaging ensemble (Zhao et al. 2019): Sequential kernel nonparametrics. cpm_wrapper() runs distribution-free sequential tests reports change detected stream (Ross 2015); kcp_wrapper() applies kernel change point analysis running statistics (mean, variance, autocorrelation, correlation) (Arlot et al. 2019; Cabrieto et al. 2018); npmojo_wrapper() detects distributional changes serial dependence (McGonigle Cho 2025): Robustness drift dependence. DeCAFS detects abrupt changes signal also drifts noise autocorrelated (Romano et al. 2022); self-normalised segmentation avoids long-run variance estimation entirely (Zhao et al. 2022); EnvCpt reports changepoints changepoint model beats trend autoregressive alternatives (Beaulieu Killick 2018): High-dimensional multivariate. inspect_wrapper() finds sparse mean changes projection (Wang Samworth 2018); ocd_wrapper() monitors high-dimensional stream online (Chen et al. 2022); geomcp_wrapper() maps observation distance angle segments (Grundy et al. 2020); multivariate ecp input flows cpt_detect() unchanged. Regression structure. strucchange_wrapper() dates Bai–Perron breaks confidence intervals (Bai Perron 1998, 2003; Zeileis et al. 2002) accepts either bare series formula; segmented_wrapper() fits continuous broken-line regressions breakpoint standard errors (Muggeo 2003, 2008): modern PELT family. fastcpd_wrapper() exposes fastcpd engine — mean, variance, mean--variance, AR/ARMA/GARCH model changepoints one interface (Li Zhang 2024):

title: ggchangepoint: A Unified Tidy Interface for Changepoint Analysis in R
text: Changepoint analysis — locating instants stochastic behaviour ordered sequence changes — one oldest problems statistics, dating back least quality-control charts Page (1954), one active: modern surveys catalogue dozens families methods (Truong et al. 2020; Aminikhanghahi Cook 2017). applications span virtually every domain produces sequential data, including genomics (Picard et al. 2005), finance (Athey et al. 2022), climate science (Haslett Raftery 1989), signal processing (Lavielle 2005). R ecosystem mirrors breadth. Penalised optimal partitioning lives changepoint (Killick Eckley 2014) fpop (Maidstone et al. 2017); wild binary segmentation wbs breakfast (Fryzlewicz 2014, 2020); multiscale inference stepR (Frick et al. 2014); Bayesian analysis bcp (Erdman Emerson 2007) ocp (Adams MacKay 2007); structural breaks strucchange (Zeileis et al. 2002); . packages excellent , returns different object, follows different indexing convention, draws (draw) plots. analyst wants compare PELT segmentation Bayesian posterior multiscale confidence set — routine task applied work — must therefore learn several APIs, reconcile several conventions, write custom plotting code . ggchangepoint removes friction. design goals : One vocabulary. single front door, cpt_detect(x, method, change_in, penalty, ...), whose arguments mean thing every engine. One result type. Every detector returns ggcpt object stable tidy contract, whatever upstream engine returned. One rendering path. Every result — point estimates, confidence intervals, fitted signals, posteriors, penalty paths — draws autoplot() extends ordinary ggplot2 layers. SMUCE (Frick, Munk Sieling, 2014) HSMUCE (Pein, Sieling Munk, 2017) give simultaneous confidence sets; Bai–Perron (strucchange) segmented give break-date CIs. visualisation-first package draw interval around changepoint behind field. Bayesian pillar mandatory. Barry–Hartigan (bcp), BOCPD (Adams MacKay, 2007; ocp), widely used BEAST ensemble (Rbeast) CRAN produce field’s signature graphics (posterior profiles, run-length heatmaps) — exactly package’s remit. Slope changes deserve exact engine. cpop (Fearnhead, Maidstone Letchford, 2019; JSS software paper 2024) CRAN canonical answer change_in = "slope" request 0.3.0 route ’s contrast. fastcpd notable newcomer. Li Zhang’s fastcpd (2024) reached CRAN 1.0.0 2026 covers mean/variance/GLM/ARMA/GARCH families one PELT-style interface — survey’s highest-priority “new package miss”. Dependence-aware methods prevent classic false positive. DeCAFS (drift + AR noise), SNSeg (self-normalisation), EnvCpt (changepoints vs trends vs memory), NP-MOJO (CptNonPar, nonparametric serial dependence) CRAN address common practical failure naive mean-shift detection. CRAN availability rules 0.3.0 plans. gfpop removed CRAN (2024) remains GitHub-; robseg FOCuS never CRAN; hdbinseg (SBS) archived. live Suggests CRAN package deferred (§5) — cpt_methods() says honestly. bcp cpm CRAN mid-2026 (brief archival episodes historically; pin versions recurs). covering/F1 one--one matching benchmark standard — audit (§6, C12–C15) shows 0.3.0 metrics module implemented inconsistently.

title: ggchangepoint: A Roadmap for the Next Release
text: C1 (critical). ecp_wrapper() fabricated changepoints -change data. changepoints, estimates = c(1, n+1) positional strip estimates[2:(length-1)] evaluated 2:1, returning reversed boundaries — ghost changepoint n (cp_value = NA) instead documented empty tibble. root cause silently dropped genuine changepoints e.agglo’s wrap-around case. Fixed value-based filtering (estimates > 1 & estimates <= n). C2 (critical). wbs_wrapper() discarded model selection claimed. default branch computed sSIC selection read cpt.th[[1]] — unrelated threshold selection — labelled result “sSIC”. Fixed read cpt.ic$ssic.penalty; manual threshold now recorded penalty actually used. C3 (major). Univariate wrappers silently flattened matrices. 100×2 matrix became 200-point series meaningless changepoints. univariate paths now error list multivariate methods; single-column matrices/data frames still work. C9 (major). cpt_detect() forward change_in . method = "", change_in = "var" ran mean contrast reported “mean”. Contrasts now mapped centrally (var → pcwsConstMeanVar, slope → pcwsLinContMean) object reports ran. C10 (major). penalty = "None" silently became default. numeric-penalty engines, unmapped strings fell NULL → engine default; "None" now resolves 0. C11 (major). cpt_penalty("sSIC") returned half SIC. “strengthened” criterion weaker BIC, -detecting wherever used; now (k(n)^{1.01}). C18 (major). signal_blocks() used absolute levels Donoho–Johnstone jumps. classic signal cumulative sum jump heights; benchmarks literature scored wrong signal. C19 (minor). t-noise sd ≈ 1.73×sd. rt(n, df) * sd sd-sd noise; now rescaled (), df <= 2 rejected.

C20 (minor). signal generators produced nonsense small n (negative length., nine zero changepoints, n changepoint); now validate minimum sizes.

title: ggchangepoint: A Roadmap for the Next Release
text: C16 (major). ggcpt_compare(layout = "facet") errored method found changepoints, silently dropped panels methods found none. Panels now come method list. Also fixed: show_ci documented unimplemented (§4 makes real); geom_cpt_ci() sat deprecated geom_errorbarh(); autoplot()’s ... silently swallowed misspelled arguments (now warns); empty ggcpt objects produced Inf-limit plots (now clean error); ggecpplot() crashed data-frame input (now plots first column message); cpt_wrapper(cp_method = "SegNeigh") always errored default penalty (now falls back SIC like dispatcher); print.ggcpt double-printed truncation message; np results now report change_in = "distribution" meanvar stays "meanvar" user’s vocabulary.

title: ggchangepoint package — ggchangepoint-package
text: ggchangepoint provides consistent S3 result class (ggcpt) changepoint detection results, broom-style methods (tidy(), glance(), augment()), ggplot2 integration via autoplot() composable geoms (geom_changepoint(), geom_cpt_segment(), geom_cpt_ci(), stat_changepoint()), unified dispatcher cpt_detect() supports thirty methods. **Detection engines.** cpt_detect() currently dispatches 31 methods across five families (run cpt_methods() live table installation status): Penalised/optimal: PELT, BinSeg, SegNeigh, AMOC     (changepoint); FPOP (fpop); CROPS penalty path     (cpt_crops()); fastcpd (fastcpd, incl. AR/ARMA/GARCH);     change--slope via CPOP (cpop). Multiscale/search: WBS (wbs), WBS2 TGUH     (breakfast), (), MOSUM incl. multiscale     (mosum), Isolate-Detect (IDetect), SMUCE/HSMUCE     confidence intervals (stepR). Nonparametric/kernel: NP (changepoint.np),     E-Divisive/E-Agglo (ecp), kernel running statistics     (kcpRS), NP-MOJO (CptNonPar), sequential CPM (cpm),     self-normalisation (SNSeg). Bayesian: Barry-Hartigan posterior (bcp), online     BOCPD (ocp), BEAST model averaging (Rbeast). Multivariate/high-dimensional regression: sparse     projection (InspectChangepoint), online ocd (ocd),     geometric mapping (changepoint.geo), Bai-Perron breaks CIs     (strucchange), broken-line regression (segmented),     changepoints-vs-autocorrelation model selection (EnvCpt),     drift+AR robust detection (DeCAFS). **Key features.** Every detector returns ggcpt object stable tibble(cp, cp_value) contract (plus engine extras ci_lower/ci_upper posterior_prob). Visualise result directly autoplot() (confidence intervals, fitted signals, multivariate facets), Bayesian displays (ggcpt_posterior(), ggcpt_runlength()), interactively via ggcpt_interactive(). Compare methods ggcpt_compare(); run panels series cpt_batch(); quantify uncertainty cpt_stability(); sweep penalties cpt_crops(). Evaluate accuracy cpt_metrics() ggcpt_eval(); simulate ground-truth data cpt_simulate() canonical test signals; cite methodology behind result cpt_cite().
